processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Steel blocks were cast via vacuum arc furnace.
Homogenization promotes uniform composition and microstructure throughout the steel blocks.
Homogenized steel subjected to step-by-step hot rolling reducing thickness to ~11 mm, followed by slow cooling in the oven.
Samples fabricated with water jet cutting machine (OMAX 2626, Kent, Washington, USA) for accurate geometries. Cylindrical specimens (∅5 x 10 mm³) used for heat treatments.
Austenitizing temperature TA = 1150 °C for S4; Table 2 lists applied TA = 1150 °C. Fig. 1(a) gives S4: 1150 °C, 1250 °C (15 min.) and a heating rate of 10 K/s.

processing_steps.method: cooling from austenitization to austempering temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cooling rate of 100 K/s from austenitization to TB, sufficiently fast to suppress intermediate phase transformations.
TB = 320 °C for S4; complete bainitic transformation time Bt = 3500 s at 320 °C. Incubation time was 50–60 s across S4 parameters. After the hold, final cooling to room temperature.

structures.overall_structure: Nano-bainitic microstructure produced for Ti-microalloyed steel S4 after austenitizing at 1150 °C and austempering at 320 °C: a markedly fine, dense sheaf/needle bainitic ferrite matrix with film-like retained austenite, needle-shaped TiMoC precipitates, strongly suppressed (Fe,M)xCy and MoC, trace αp (<1.0 %) and minor dark angular AlN particles.

phases_present.morphology: markedly finer, denser sheaf/needle bainitic morphology; nano-bainitic lamellar thickness Lt(t) = 36 nm (SD 12)

defects.lattice_distortion: εγ = 0.58 %, εα = 0.60 % (XRD Rietveld micro-strains); no significant ε difference observed between the phases at this condition
Absence of micro-defects within the Ti–Mo–C complex carbides

precipitates.distribution: needle-shaped/elongated precipitates with longitudinal alignment (formed during cooling after casting and subsequent hot forming); the fine dense structure at TB 320 °C is labelled 'TiMoC precipitates' in SEM and confirmed by EDX (Fe-depleted, C/Ti/Mo-enriched)
less present in S4 than in S1, S2, S3 due to the suppressing effect of TiMoC
dark angular particle observed by SEM in S4 at TA 1150 °C / TB 350 °C

defect_interactions.interaction_type: bainitic sheaf impingement at increased phase boundaries
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: TiMoC accelerates bainite nucleation (shorter incubation 50–60 s), but the increased number of phase boundaries causes bainitic sheaf impingement that slows the later progression of bainite transformation in S4 compared to S1 and S2.

interfaces.phase_evolution: TiMoC forms during the cooling phase after casting and is aligned longitudinally by subsequent hot forming (secondary precipitation negligible during austempering); TiMoC suppresses the formation of (Fe,M)xCy, MoC and possibly κ-carbide. No new secondary precipitates were detected during austempering (within SEM resolution), consistent with TTP calculations.
interfaces.interface_notes: At TB 320 °C the finer, denser sheaf/needle structure gives a denser interface network; the fine prior austenite grain size at 1150 °C causes impingement, which is why a 1250 °C schedule was additionally tested.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: ASTM E8 sub-size round specimens (12.5 mm gauge length, 2.5 mm diameter, 7 mm shoulder length)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile specimens heat-treated using the DIL 805A dilatometer applying the thermal cycle of Fig. 1(a) (TA 1150 °C, TB 320 °C); tested on a Zwick/Roell universal testing machine (250 kN load cell).
Ms determined by rapid cooling at 100 K/s from TA 1150 °C using DIL 805A dilatometer.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: DIL 805A dilatometer (TA Instruments, New Castle, DE, USA)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Heating 10 K/s to TA, cooling 100 K/s to TB; RLC (%) vs time/temperature curves
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine transformation finish time Bt (plateau onset of RLC curve) and Ms (tangent-intersection of cooling RLC curve)
characterization_methods.key_findings: S4 at TB 320 °C completed bainitic transformation at Bt = 3500 s; Ms = 305 °C after austenitizing at 1150 °C; incubation 50–60 s.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss SEM (Carl Zeiss AG, Jena, Germany) with EDX (Oxford Instruments, Abingdon, UK); gold sputter coating of etched samples
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SEM micrographs at 10 µm scale; EDX elemental mapping (Fe Kα1, C Kα1,2, Ti Kα1, Mo Lα1)
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal bainitic morphology and identify chemistry of precipitates in S4
characterization_methods.key_findings: S4 TA 1150 °C / TB 320 °C shows a markedly finer, denser sheaf/needle structure labelled TiMoC precipitates; EDX mapping confirms needle-shaped Ti–Mo carbides (Fe-depleted, C/Ti/Mo-enriched); a dark angular AlN particle is seen at 1150/350 °C.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Malvern Panalytical Empyrean diffractometer, Cu X-ray tube, 40 kV/40 mA, PIXcel 1D detector (TU Clausthal Institute of Non-Metallic Materials)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Cu Kα radiation; intensities from (111)γ, (200)γ, (220)γ, (311)γ peaks; ASTM E975-13 guidelines
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine retained austenite volume fraction Vγ and phase micro-strains (εγ, εα)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss AG, Jena, Germany; etched with 6 % Nital solution
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: LOM at 1050 °C and at selected TA 1150 °C, 100 µm scale bars
characterization_methods.purpose: Verify polygonal ferrite (αp) content after austenitizing
characterization_methods.key_findings: S4 contained a visibly higher amount of αp at 1050 °C but only a trace level (<1 %) at 1150 °C.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zwick/Roell universal testing machine (250 kN load cell, Zwick Roell Group, Ulm, Germany)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: ASTM E8 sub-size round specimens (12.5 mm gauge length, 2.5 mm diameter, 7 mm shoulder length), heat-treated in DIL 805A dilatometer
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure UTS, Rp0.2 and elongation of the heat-treated conditions
characterization_methods.key_findings: S4 at TA 1150 °C, TB 320 °C: UTS 1360 MPa, El 10 %, PSE 13,600 MPa·%.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: MatCalc (Version: 6.01 (rel 1.003), Institute of Materials Science and Technology, TU Wien, Wien, Austria)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Equilibrium step calculations and precipitation kinetics (TTP diagrams) for cooling rate 100 K/s; S4 systems Ti-Mo-C and (Fe,M)xCy
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine ferrite-free TA and carbide-dissolution Tcd; simulate precipitation of TiMoC and (Fe,M)xCy
characterization_methods.key_findings: S4 ferrite-free TA = 1016 °C, Tcd = 1134 °C; only S4 has a resolved TiMoC system that retards/suppresses (Fe,M)xCy; no new secondary precipitates during austempering.

computational_details.simulation_method: equilibrium phase calculations (step calculation method) to obtain ferrite-free TA and carbide-dissolution temperature Tcd
computational_details.software_used: MatCalc Version 6.01 (rel 1.003), Institute of Materials Science and Technology, TU Wien, Wien, Austria
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Synergy of phases fcc, bcc, liquid, κ-carbide, hcp carbide, AlN, TiCN–TiMoC system considered for equilibrium and kinetic calculations
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Standard step calculation method over temperature range (S4 axis begins at 400 °C); alloy composition of S4 (Table 1)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Simulated ferrite-free TA (1016 °C) below the applied TA 1150 °C; consistent with LOM showing only trace αp (<1 %) at 1150 °C.

computational_details.simulation_method: precipitation kinetics simulation (Time-Temperature-Precipitation, TTP diagrams) using heterogeneous nucleation theory
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Ti-Mo-C and (Fe,M)xCy carbide systems; heterogeneous nucleation considering dislocation and grain boundary sites, ortho-equilibrium transformation, and volumetric misfit; κ-carbides treated as fixed phase fractions
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Cooling rate 100 K/s; T_A: 1250 °C, 1150 °C (900 s); T_B lines at 350 °C (Bt: 2600 s–3000 s) and 320 °C (Bt: 3500 s); two grey-shaded precipitation bands labelled TiMoC and (Fe,M)xCy
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: TTP results are compatible with SEM observations: (Fe,M)xCy initial nucleation between 700–950 °C is suppressed by the counter-coarsening effect of TiMoC in S4; no new secondary precipitates detected during austempering within SEM resolution.

computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Vγ = (1 − Vc)(Iγ/Rγ)/[(Iα/Rα)+(Iγ/Rγ)]; MatCalc equilibrium phase diagrams used to assess carbide phase fraction (Vc)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Integrated intensities of α and γ peaks; Vc from MatCalc equilibrium phase fractions
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Applied to determine Vγ of the S4 (TA 1150 °C, TB 320 °C) condition = 26 %.

analytical_models.equation_role: Computes Vγ from integrated α/γ XRD intensities corrected for carbide fraction Vc

parameters.name: Iα, Iγ
parameters.value: integrated intensities of α and γ

analytical_models.model_note: MatCalc equilibrium phase diagrams used to obtain Vc by treating (1 − Vc) as the total (bainitic ferrite + γr) fraction.

unmapped_findings: S4 (TA 1150 °C, TB 320 °C): product of strength and elongation (PSE) = 13,600 MPa·%, the highest PSE value reported for S4 under TA 1150 °C austenitizing in Section 3.3 (b0064); no dedicated PSE field exists in the schema.
Incubation time for S4 was 50–60 s across all parameters (including TB 320 °C), the shortest among the investigated steels except S5 (Section 3.2, b0057).

The paper reports an internal inconsistency for S4: Section 3.3 (b0064) attributes El = 10 % and PSE = 13,600 MPa·%/13,380 MPa·% to TB 320 °C and 350 °C respectively, whereas Section 3.4.4 (b0091) and the Conclusion (b0111) associate El ≈ 10 %/maximum 12 % and the best PSE ≈ 13.6 GPa·% with TA 1150 °C / TB 350 °C. The assigned values here (UTS 1360 MPa, El 10 %, PSE 13,600 MPa·%) follow the explicit pairing in b0064, consistent with the process snapshot noting the highest elongation (~10 %) at TB 320 °C.

Hardness: HV30 values across all studied conditions ranged between 450 and 500 HV30, with higher values at lower TB except for steel S4 (Section 3.3, b0061). The per-condition hardness values printed in Fig. 7 (464, 497, 465, 500, 443, 457, 464, 479, 467, 459, 493 HV30) cannot be unambiguously mapped to the S4 TB 320 °C condition, so no hardness value is assigned to this sample.
S4 reached the best average and maximum elongation of 10 % and 12 % (Section 3.4.4, b0091); the maximum El of 12 % is not assigned to a specific TB in that statement.

MatCalc predicted complete dissolution of MC-type (Fe,M)xCy carbides near 1134 °C for S4 (Section 3.1, b0033) — this is the S4 carbide-dissolution temperature Tcd agreeing with the Tcd value in Fig. 4.
Yield strength (Rp0.2) values are reported only as extremes across all steels (max 1225 MPa for S1 at 300 °C and min 945 MPa for S3 at 270 °C), so no Rp0.2 is assigned to S4 (Section 3.3, b0061).

No κ-carbide (E21 perovskite-type) structures were directly observed microscopically due to the limited Mn content (~1 wt.%), and the remaining κ-carbides are presumed to exist as nanoscale embedded non-stoichiometric L12-type structures (Section 3.4.3, b0085) — general to the steel family, not a measured S4 phase fraction.
